frontier.hypothesis: The last two instructions close by making `sum_sq` lose global.c's priority sort from the DENOMINATOR side (live length) rather than the numerator (references), so the small arm's LUT byte can go back to its own short-lived pseudo and land in $v0.
frontier.mechanism: allocno_compare ranks allocnos on a function of allocno_n_refs and allocno_live_length. The numerator side is measured flat: every reference the copy's variable can honestly take, other than the small arm's byte, costs the seats it touches (5, 4, 4, 13, 13, 13). The denominator has never been attacked - lengthening sum_sq's live range, or shortening the copy's while keeping it a cross-block (global) allocno, would flip the same comparison without borrowing a register that shows in the bytes.
frontier.next_probe: Read allocno_n_refs / allocno_live_length for both allocnos out of the .lreg and .greg dumps of tmp/grind/func_80018094/s9/m1.c (loses the sort) versus n1.c (wins it) - they differ only in the boost, so the two arrays bracket the threshold. Then spell denominator-side C on the n13 chassis: move the `lut = sum_sq;` copy later (it is currently the first statement inside the outer wrap, before the `sum_sq < 0x400` test - the target's copy is in the branch's delay slot, i.e. as late as possible), and try ending sum_sq's live range differently in the tail.

frontier.hypothesis: The s9b gate shape generalises: a residual that is a cse-deleted copy across a two-arm branch can be closed by respelling the fallthrough arm as `if (cond) { do { ...; goto L; } while (0); }`.
frontier.mechanism: The lever is a property of tools/gcc-2.7.2/cse.c's follow-jumps gate, not of this function: the loop-end note between the arm's BARRIER and the else label is what stops cse from extending the block. Nine sessions here treated 'cse deletes the copy' as a class kill (s6, s9a H42, predicate cse.c:8102); that kill is now scoped to bodies whose arms are spelled `if/else`.
frontier.next_probe: When a sibling ledger reports a copy that 'cse always deletes', transplant this shape before re-deriving. Within this function, re-audit the s6/s9a class kill H42 - it is instance-scoped under the new evidence, and its predicate line (cse.c:8102) points at the block scan rather than at the gate at 8100-8125.

frontier.hypothesis: The Judge-FAILed tied-operand lineage (s9a b4 -> f1) is fully superseded and should not be revisited: everything it bought is now bought honestly.
frontier.mechanism: The tied `"=r"(lut)` / `"1"(sum_sq)` pair existed only to make reload materialise the pre-island copy. The s9b gate materialises the same copy from ordinary C, and the seat it landed on ($a0) is reproduced by the priority-sort boost. The zero body's other two devices (sp_tmp[4] oversized locals, the outer do-while(0) wrap) are carried unchanged in candidate.c.
frontier.next_probe: None needed; recorded so a later session does not re-file a ruling-request on the operand. The Judge's binding constraint stands: no extra output, tied, or clobber operand may be added to any __asm__ in this function.

judge_constraints: The LZC island's operand list must stay exactly the granted form (`: "=m"(sp_tmp[0]) : "r"(sum_sq) : "$2", "$12"`); no extra output, tied/matching ("0"/"1"), or clobber operand may be added to any __asm__ in this function to make the compiler materialise a copy. The pre-island `move $a0,$a1` must come from ordinary C or the function stays INCOMPLETE.
